newsitem.title: UK: IPE natgas untraded but prompt bids, offers down.
newsitem.headline: IPE natgas untraded but prompt bids, offers down.

text.p: The IPE natural gas futures market was untraded on Monday morning, although bids and offers were posted in all months and were close in some months, especially August and September.
Front month July was bid at 9.50 pence a therm and offered at 9.95 pence, down from a settlement level of 9.995 pence on Friday evening.
"Most people are in meetings, working out their weekly programmes," said a futures broker.
He added that prices had "slimmed down" last week, and that when details of the Transco tender appeared late in the week, some said that its impact had already been factored into the market.
Even so, prices slipped on Friday evening, and the trend continued weaker on Monday morning with offers in the front months below the previous settlement level.

And although there were reasonably tight bid/offer spreads in some of the front months, January and February remained a full one penny apart. "Down the curve we're going back to our bad old ways," said a broker.
